text:
anya: Quick FYI — our canary run of tundra-micro-int4 (ptq) started showing a 3.8% spike in funcall parse failures compared to the float baseline. Happening only on streaming responses, not batch. :thinking:

sam: Ugh. Are these full JSON malforms or schema mismatches?

anya: Mostly malforms — truncated suffixes and occasional stray commas. Sampled 200 failures; ~70% end with partial JSON (missing closing brace) and ~20% have extra trailing comma.

lee: Can you paste a minimal example?

anya: Sure, from the canary logs (sanitized):
```
{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"title": "Login bug", "assignee": "ops",},
...stream cut...
```

maria: That looks like a streaming cutoff — maybe kv-cache or tokenization length change after quant? Any tokenizer deltas between tundra-micro-int4 and baseline?

sam: We didn't change token vocab. But PTQ sometimes shifts tokenization at boundaries due to rounding in logits ordering -> different EOS placement. Could cause earlier termination.

lee: Good point. Also check if continuous batching/tokens-per-request distribution changed — longer tails can be cut by the runtime's streaming chunker.

anya: I pulled the request/response pairs. For the same prompt, float model produced final tokens: `..."}` 
` while int4 variant produced `...","` then stop.

maria: CI-bot, can you run the structured-output sanity check on the last 500 canary samples for tundra-micro-int4 and baseline and post metrics?

ci-bot: Running structured-output-sanity (v2) on 500 samples for tundra-micro-int4. ETA ~2m.

sam: In parallel, can infra dump the streaming chunk sizes and last-token logits for a few reproducer seeds? If the model's highest-prob token changes, our streaming heuristic might think EOS arrived.

lee: I've seen this before when quantized top-k behavior flips ordering for near-ties. Our parser assumes full JSON arrives or we retry — but retries are being rate-limited; that also explains the spike since retried calls are insufficient.

anya: Short-term mitigation idea: enable our "append-EOF" guard for canaries (inject a small heuristic that appends `"}` when trailing token looks like mid-JSON and retry) — not ideal but buys time. Thoughts?

maria: Prefer to add a non-invasive heal: try a lightweight postprocess that attempts minimal JSON repair (close braces, strip trailing commas) and then attempt a parse. Flag repaired results so we can track regressions. Keep the original raw output in logs.

sam: Agree. Make it opt-in for the canary traffic only. Also add a metric for "healed_parse_success_rate" so we know how often it's used.

lee: Also add a canary run with kv-cache disabled (single-turn) to see if caching is amplifying suffix truncation. If it stops happening, caching interaction is suspect.

anya: Plan recap: (1) ci-bot results, (2) enable opt-in json-healer on canary + metric, (3) run kv-cache-off canary, (4) collect last-token logits and streaming chunk traces. I'll coordinate.

maria: I'll prepare a tiny repair lib and a dashboard tile for healed_parse_success_rate and healed_by_type (close_brace, strip_comma, pad_eos).

ci-bot: structured-output-sanity results: tundra-micro-int4: parse_success=92.1%, healed_success=3.6%, final_failure=4.3%. baseline (float): parse_success=96.0%, healed_success=0.5%, final_failure=3.5%. Full report uploaded to /canary/reports/tundra-micro-int4/1779998881.json

sam: That confirms partial mitigation by healing but real regression vs baseline still ~3.9% relative.

lee: Reminder to check tokenization alignment tests — run `token-align --compare tundra-micro-int4 baseline --samples 1000` and dump diffs.

anya: I'll kick that off. If token alignment diffs concentrate on punctuation/EOS tokens, we likely have PTQ-induced tie flips.

maria: If PTQ is the cause we should also test small calibration tweaks (per-channel vs per-tensor) and re-run quickly; those can shift borderline logits back. I'll queue a quick quant sweep (3 configs) on the same canary dataset.

sam: Nice. For release gating: hold tundra-micro-int4 from broader rollout until healed_success + parse_success combined >= baseline parse_success - 0.5%. In practice that means we need parse_success >= 95.5% without relying heavily on repair.

anya: Agreed. I'll log an incident-style note in #incidents if numbers don't improve after the quant sweep. Thanks all, will post updates. :thumbsup:
